title: Notice Given Before the Original Slot — Late-Change Fee, Outpatient Surgery Package
content:
Under the Riverbend Self-Pay Package Price - Outpatient Surgery terms of Good Faith & Price Estimates, the notice the patient gave before the original slot date decides how much of the fee basis of a late surgical move is kept.

**Term.** The notice days run from the change date to the original slot date, the change date not counted and the slot date counted. Four to six notice days keep one half (0.5, that is 50 percent) of the fee basis; one to three notice days keep three quarters (0.75) of it; a change on the slot date itself (zero notice days) keeps all of it. The change date and the original slot date are read from Appointment Scheduling: the patient's Outpatient Procedure Appointment that shows cancelled by the patient gives its cancellation date as the change date and its scheduled date as the original slot date, the first such appointment the record lists being read where there are several.

| Notice days | Share of the fee basis kept |
|---|---|
| 4 to 6 | one half (0.5) |
| 1 to 3 | three quarters (0.75) |
| 0 (change on the slot date) | all of it |

## Boundaries (hypothetical dates, slot on the 20th)

- Cancelled on the 16th: 4 notice days, one half kept.
- Cancelled on the 17th: 3 notice days, three quarters kept.
- Cancelled on the 19th: 1 notice day, three quarters kept.
- Cancelled on the 20th: 0 notice days, all kept.
